questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of ‘untouchability’ and prohibits its practice in any shape or form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 17**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 17 of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of **‘untouchability**’ and prohibits its practice in any shape or form.
 
• In fact, the enforcement of any disability arising out of **untouchability shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law**.
 
• In fact, this is one of the few **fundamental rights which is available to individuals**.
 
• To make the untouchability law further strong, parliament passed an Untouchability (offenses) Act in 1955.
 
• However, this act was further amended and also renamed in the year 1976 as the Protection of the Civil Rights Act, of 1955.​

questions.question: How many fundamental duties are listed in the Indian Constitution as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Indian Constitution lists** **11 fundamental duties** as of** 2022, **which are outlined in **Article 51A of Part IV-A of the Constitution.**
 
• The 11th fundamental duty was added in 2002 by the **86th Amendment Act.**
 
• This duty mandates that parents or guardians provide educational opportunities for their children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• **The fundamental duties include**:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **correct about Fundamental Duties?

options.text: They were included by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
They are mentioned under Article 51A of the Constitution.
Their inclusion in the Constitution was inspired by the American Constitution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Their inclusion in the Constitution was inspired by the American Constitution__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Fundamental Duties Of the Indian Constitution

 
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties is inspired by the Constitution of Russia. *Hence, Option 4 is not correct.*
 
• These were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. 
 
• Originally 10 in number, one more duty was added through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. 
 
• All eleven duties are listed in Article 51-A of the Constitution (the sole Article in Part-IV-A).
 
• The fundamental duties serve as a reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they have also to be quite conscious of the duties they owe to their country, their society and to their fellow citizens.
 
• However, like the Directive Principles, the duties are also non-justiciable in nature.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 75 of the Constitution of India** delineates** the process of appointing the Prime Minister** by** the President of India, **who also appoints other Ministers upon the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Additionally, this article specifies the following provisions:
 
 
• Ministers serve at the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Council of Ministers is accountable to the House of the People.
 
• The President administers oaths of office and secrecy to Ministers before assuming their duties.
 
 
 
• Moreover, the Prime Minister assumes leadership of the advisory committee and holds responsibility for appointing administrative officials such as** members and the Chairman of the Finance Commission, UPSC, CAG, Attorney General, etc.**
 
• Additionally, the Prime Minister acts as the principal liaison between the President and the council of ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 73** of the Constitution of India grants the central government executive authority over subjects within the purview of Parliament's legislative powers.
 
• **Article 74** establishes a Council of Ministers to aid the President in fulfilling their responsibilities. The Prime Minister leads this Council of Ministers.
 
• Under **Article 76,** the President appoints the Attorney General for India, who serves at the pleasure of the President.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 141**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 141** of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.
 
• This article ensures the uniformity and consistency of legal principles across the country.
 
• The Supreme Court's decisions serve as precedents that lower courts must follow.
 
• This provision helps maintain a cohesive and integrated judicial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Supreme Court of India** is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It has the power of judicial review to ensure the constitutionality of laws and acts passed by the legislature and executive.
 
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 34 judges, appointed by the President of India.
 
• Decisions made by the Supreme Court are binding on all other courts in India, as per **Article 141**.
 
• The Supreme Court also has the authority to interpret the Constitution and is often involved in adjudicating significant constitutional matters.
 
• This article ensures that the law of the land is uniformly applied, preventing conflicting judgments from different courts.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution lays the condition that the President, once elected, shall NOT be a member of the either House of Parliament or state legislature?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Article 59.**

**Article 59 in the Constitution of Indi**a

__
 
• Conditions of President's office
 
• (1) The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State be elected President, he shall be deemed to have vacated his seat in that House on the date on which he enters upon his office as President.
 
• (2) The President shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• (3) The President shall be entitled without payment of rent to the use of his official residences and shall be also entitled to such emoluments, allowances and privileges as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such emoluments, allowances and privileges as are specified in the Second Schedule.
 
• (4) The emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during his term of office.

questions.question: Which of the following directs the State to provide ‘Equal justice and free legal aid’?

options.text: Part VI of the Indian Constitution
Part V of the Indian Constitution
Part VII of the Indian Constitution
Part IV of the Indian Constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV of the Indian Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Directive Principles of our State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• The DPSP is covered under** Articles 36 to 51** of the Indian constitution.
 
• According to **Article 39A**, the State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes or in any other way, to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
 
• The DPSP is borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part V **of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions related to the Union Government under articles 52 to 151.
 
• **Part VI **of the Indian Constitution deals with the provision related to the State Government under articles 152 to 237.
 
• **Part VII **of the Indian Constitution has been repealed by the 7th constitutional amendment act 1956. It was regarding Part B states which were princely states or group of princely states

questions.question: Which of the following Acts prevents disrespect to the National Flag and National Anthem?

options.text: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act of 1971** serves to safeguard the integrity of the **National Flag, National Anthem, and Constitution of India. **This legislation imposes penalties on individuals who display disrespect towards these national symbols.
 
• Offenders can face imprisonment for up to three years, a monetary fine, or both. The Act also regulates the proper hoisting, usage, and exhibition of the Indian National Flag.
 
• Among its provisions are prohibitions against allowing the flag to touch the ground or be draped over vehicles, buildings, or other objects. Additionally, intentional display of the flag with the saffron color facing downwards is deemed inappropriate.
 
• The Supreme Court has clarified that respectful standing during the National Anthem, even if not sung, does not constitute a violation of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Part IVA of the Indian Constitution** outlines the fundamental duties of Indian citizens, which include adhering to the Constitution, respecting its principles and institutions, as well as honoring the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• The corresponding Act elaborates on the penalties for contravening Article 51Aa of the Constitution.
 
• According to this Act, individuals holding high-ranking positions such as the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and other government officials can face disqualification if found guilty of violating the Constitution, as per sections 7 and 8(k) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• In instances where the judiciary annuls unconstitutional actions of the executive, these actions are deemed as written acts visible to the public, thereby constituting contempt of the Constitution of India or its provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the relationship between the Prime Minister and the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 75 **outlines the following provisions:

 
 
• The President appoints the Prime Minister, and the other Ministers are appointed by the President based on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Ministers serve at the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively accountable to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• Before assuming office, a Minister must take the oaths of office and secrecy administered by the President, as outlined in the Third Schedule.
 
• A Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament for a consecutive six-month period ceases to be a Minister at the end of that period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 45 **of the Indian Constitution falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). It mandates that the state should ensure free and compulsory education for all children up to the age of 14.
 
• **Article 25 **of the Indian Constitution enshrines the freedom of conscience and the right to practice, profess, and propagate religion for all citizens.
 
• **Article 35 **grants exclusive legislative authority to Parliament to enact laws concerning Articles 16(3), 32(3), 33, and 34.

questions.question: As per Article 361 of the Constitution of India, who among the following shall NOT be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** ​Governor.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 361 of the Constitution of India, a **criminal proceeding cannot be instituted in a court against the Governor** during his term of office.
 
• The President or Governor, while in the office is not personally responsible for any court for the exercise and execution of their powers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State:
 
 
• **shall not be answerable to any court **for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office.
 
• If Any act done or purporting to be done by him in the exercise and performance of those powers and duties:
 
 
 
• **No criminal proceedings** whatsoever shall be instituted or continued against :
 
 
• the** President, or the Governor** of a State, in any court during his term of office.
 
 
 
• **No civil proceedings** in which relief is claimed against the President, or the Governor of a State:
 
 
• shall be instituted during his term of office in any court in respect of any act done or purporting to be done by him

questions.question: Which among the following is INCORRECT about the salient features of the 73rd Amendment Act?

options.text: The Act gives a Constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions.
It contains 29 functional items of the Panchayats and deals with Article 243 to 243(O).
The Act has added the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.
The Act corresponds to Part III of the Constitution of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**The Act corresponds to Part III of the Constitution of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 73rd Amendment Act** added **Part IX** to the Constitution of India, titled **"The Panchayats,"** which covers** Articles 243 to 243O**.
 
• Alongside Part IX, the amendment also introduced the **Eleventh Schedule**, which lists 29 items for panchayats to address.
 
• The amendment established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system for local self-government, consisting of **Zila Parishad** at the district level, **Block Samiti** at the block level, and **Gram Panchayat **at the village level.
 
• The amendment mandates state governments to adopt the new Panchayati Raj system, except in areas excluded from its application.
 
• The amendment does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, as well as certain other regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State governments** are constitutionally mandated to adopt the** new Panchayati Raj system** as prescribed by the act.
 
• The act establishes the** Gram Sabha** as the cornerstone of the Panchayati Raj framework. In accordance with the act, each state is required to implement a three-tier Panchayati Raj system, encompassing village, intermediate, and district levels.
 
• All members of the Panchayats at the village, intermediate, and district levels must be elected directly by the populace.
 
• The act stipulates that the chairpersons of Panchayats at the intermediate and district levels must be elected indirectly, chosen from among the elected members.
 
• The act also mandates the reservation of at least one-third of the total seats for women.

questions.question: In which year did the 44th Amendment remove the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 44th Amendment to the Constitution**, enacted in 1978, brought significant changes to India's legal framework. Notably, it removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights and reclassified it as a simple legal right under Article 300 A.
 
• This amendment was introduced as a response to the amendments made under the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, which had altered several provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act aimed to reverse these changes and protect the rights of citizens against potential future infringements by the majority.
 
• It's important to note that the 44th Amendment Act was introduced as a bill under the 45th Amendment Bill in 1978.
 
• Its enactment was seen as crucial in safeguarding the interests of the nation and ensuring the preservation of fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 44th Amendment Act of 1978** was a significant step in restoring balance to India's constitutional framework.
 
• It reversed a provision introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, which had granted the government extensive power to amend the Constitution at will under Article 368.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act effectively nullified this unchecked authority, ensuring that future constitutional amendments would be subject to proper scrutiny and safeguards.
 
• Additionally, the 44th Amendment Act reclassified the Right to Property, previously enshrined as a Fundamental Right under Article 31, as a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This change reflected a shift in the constitutional perspective on property rights, aligning them more closely with other legal rights while still affording protection to property owners.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution are mentioned in which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** are mentioned in **Article 51 A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976**.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: By which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act was the 11th fundamental duty added to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Eighty-sixth Amendment to the Constitution of India** introduced the **Right to Education for children** aged six to fourteen years, along with Early Childhood Care up to the age of six.
 
• This amendment included the insertion of Article 21A, establishing the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
 
• Additionally, it replaced Article 45, which pertained to Early Childhood Education under the Directive Principles of State Policy. Furthermore, the amendment amended Article 51A, which outlines Fundamental Duties, to incorporate a new obligation for parents.
 
• The newly added duty mandates parents to ensure education for their children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This duty is enshrined as the 11th fundamental duty, emphasizing the importance of providing educational opportunities to children during this crucial period of development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Constitution (87th Amendment) Act, 2003,** brought about changes to the Constitution of India by replacing the 1950 national census as the basis for the delimitation of constituencies of the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
 
• **The Constitution (Eighty-eighth Amendment) Act, 2003, **introduced on March 7, 2003 and added service tax to the Union List and granted Parliament the authority to enact laws concerning taxes on specific services.
 
• **The 85th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2001** introduced the concept of "consequential seniority" in the promotion of government servants belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
